faq.q: What is the origin of Ibraheem?
faq.a: Ibraheem is associated with Arabic. Ibraheem is Arabic إِبْرَاهِيم (Ibrāhīm), the Qur'anic form of Abraham, a prophet and the name of a Qur'anic sura. The source gloss 'Father of Nations' is unsupported; the name is a proper name. Same name as ibrah, ibrahem, ibrahim and ibrhim.
Yes — the underlying form إبراهيم is Arabic.

faq.a: In Persian, Ibraheem is rendered ابراهیم and carries the sense ابراهیم، صورت قرآنی ابراهیم.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Ibraheem, ibraheem. Script forms are إبراهيم, ابراهیم, ابراہیم, इब्राहीम.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
